title: ELSE branch leaks §4.2 key text when fraud_signals/form_session is a JSON *string* (double-encoded corrupt row) — the guard comment's 'cannot leak' claim is false for that shape
evidence: SQL lines 38-49: "when any level is not an object the form_session key path cannot exist, so passing the result through verbatim cannot leak the §4.2 keys." / "CASE WHEN result IS NULL THEN '' WHEN jsonb_typeof(result) = 'object' AND jsonb_typeof(result -> 'fraud_signals') = 'object' AND jsonb_typeof(result -> 'fraud_signals' -> 'form_session') = 'object' THEN (result #- '{fraud_signals,form_session,referee_ip}' #- '{fraud_signals,form_session,referee_user_agent}')::text ELSE result::text END AS result"
detail: If a corrupt row stores fraud_signals or form_session as a JSON string containing escaped JSON (e.g. "fraud_signals":"{\"referee_ip\":\"203.0.113.7\"}"), jsonb_typeof = 'string' routes to ELSE and the escaped key text + raw IP ride the wire inside the result string field. No current writer produces this shape (all server-built gleam JSON), so it is corrupt-row-only.
recommended_fix: Deep-strip the text: in ELSE, regexp-replace the escaped key markers (or the raw IP/UA substrings) from result::text, or add a guard that treats string-typed levels as strip-required; update the comment.
